notes.2.29: In 2.34 the text reads 'petita' ('sought'); taken as perita ('skilled'), which the sense requires. *tucceta* (2.42), rendered 'meat dishes', is a rich meat preparation of uncertain kind.
notes.5.177: 'Herod's days' (5.180) is generally taken as a Jewish festival kept at Rome; which one is not certain.

nodes.text: Jupiter? Or what is the fee with which you have bought the gods'
little ears? With lungs and greasy guts?
Look: a grandmother, or an aunt who fears the gods, from the cradle
has lifted the boy, and his forehead and wet little lips
with the infamous finger and with purifying spittle beforehand
she purifies, skilled at checking the burning eyes;
then she jiggles him in her hands, and her meagre hope, with suppliant prayer,
sends now into the estates of Licinus, now into the mansions of Crassus:
'May a king and queen want him for a son-in-law; may the girls
snatch at him; whatever he treads on, may it turn to a rose.'
But I do not entrust my prayers to a nurse; refuse
her these things, Jupiter, even though she asks you dressed in white!
You ask for strength for your sinews and a body that will stay faithful in old age:
so be it, go on; but great platters and fat meat dishes
chalk-whitened ambition? Keep watch, and pour chickpeas lavishly
on the brawling crowd, so that our Floralia can be
remembered by old men in the sun! What is finer? But when
Herod's days have come, and at the greasy window
the lamps set out in rows have spewed a fatty fog,
carrying violets, and, embracing a red dish,
the tail of a tuna swims, and the white jar swells with wine,
you move your lips silently and turn pale at the circumcised sabbaths.
Then black *lemures* [ghosts of the dead] and the dangers from a broken egg,
then the huge *galli* [eunuch priests of Cybele] and the one-eyed priestess with her sistrum
have struck into you gods who swell up bodies, unless
you have tasted the prescribed head of garlic three times in the morning.
Say these things among the varicose-veined centurions,
and at once huge Pulfenius laughs a coarse laugh
